text:
We chose MMSU student commuters as the users
for our design thinking project.

We explored their daily travel challenges to
design an IT solution that helps them plan
when, where and what to ride.
Project framing based on the user request and 195ppt.pdf. The project applies design thinking to MMSU student commuters.

name:
100 eligible student commuters

104 subm
text:
1. Walk us through a typical daily commute from start to finish for you.

2. Can you describe a specific moment during your commute this week when you felt completely stuck or delayed?

3. What is the most challenging, unpredictable, or exhausting part of your travel routine?

4. How do you currently decide when to leave, what routes or rides to take, or how to handle unexpected delays?

5. If you had a magic wand to change one thing about your current commuting process, what would it be and why?

Source: supplied CSV, substantive questions I–V. Also verified in Google Forms: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1liEG3PRR3uXq0MT-cCLoXSEfarbTrqgJ3puwW15mKtA/edit#responses . Consent and year-level questions omitted as requested.

name: Need: clearer route, fare and departure
text:
MMSU student commuters need accessible,
reliable transport information to decide
when to leave and which ride to take.

59.5% described waiting or availability problems.
28.4% (21/74) wanted transport information,
tracking or arrival information.

How might we make commute decisions clearer?

name: Feedback note
text: Qualitative prototype feedback. Evaluator count was not supplied.

Source: 195ppt.pdf, pages 2–3. The document reports positive feedback on route navigation, UI organization, navigation flow and step-by-step actions, plus requests for more notable stops and an indicator of the jeep whereabouts. No evaluator sample size, raw evaluation responses, or percentages were supplied. These are documented qualitative findings, not results calculated from the 74-response needs survey. Proposed actions: expand the stop list and clarify the vehicle marker and status on the tracking screen.

name:
Questions & answers

Research, design ch
text:
Questions and answers

Research, design choices and the app

PRESENTER: Jeiwinfrey
TIME: 30 seconds

MMSU CommuteHub brings our Design Thinking and UI/UX lessons into one commute planning experience. We started with student commuters' concerns and designed features to help them compare rides, choose a pickup, and plan around class. Through clear information, meaningful illustrations, and helpful feedback, we aim to make commute decisions easier for MMSU students. On behalf of our group, thank you for your time and attention. We are now ready for your questions.
